disqualifyingIssues: Major dropped narrative beats (illness details, doctor order, sack loneliness, full fairy transformation)
Over-condensed structure that crams or skips source events
evaluations.rationale: Severely abridged summary that omits core source sequences and reduces the story to thin narrator bridges; scenes are not broken into discrete 5-10s visual beats and character re-appearances lack locked descriptions, rendering it unusable for clip production.

Nearly complete, accurate translation of every major book beat and line of dialogue with concrete, single-location visual actions ideal for short AI clips; character looks are established early and held; only weakness is total absence of explicit music/sound-bed prompts.

Most exhaustive and precise adaptation: every source beat, sensory detail and line is preserved as discrete, camera-ready actions with consistent, lockable character descriptions (Boy fair hair/nightshirt, Nana starched apron, Rabbit progressive shabbiness); emotional arcs are crystal-clear for later music scoring even without explicit cues.

disqualifyingIssues: Invented toy dialogue and spoken tear monologue
Re-ordered and partially dropped Christmas/Skin-Horse setup
evaluations.rationale: Invented proper names and dialogue plus structural reordering trigger severe fidelity penalty; remaining visuals are serviceable but the script cannot be green-lit as a faithful adaptation.

disqualifyingIssues: Major dropped beats (full Skin Horse speech, detailed illness, complete fairy sequence)
Overly skeletal scenes that collapse multiple source events
evaluations.rationale: Bare-bones condensation that loses most of the book’s emotional texture and visual specificity; too many multi-beat summaries and missing character locks make it unsuitable for per-clip AI generation.

Faithful, well-paced coverage of virtually all source incidents with clear visual staging and authentic dialogue; character descriptions are solid and recurring; only minor shortfall is lack of music/sound prompts and slightly less granular action lines than top contenders.

disqualifyingIssues: Jumbled chronology and wrong locations (wild rabbits appear in spring garden)
Major invented/reordered events and incomplete transformation/ending
Near-total drop of source coverage and character visual locks
evaluations.rationale: Broken structure that misplaces key scenes, invents dialogue and truncates the climax; unusable as either faithful adaptation or clip-ready screenplay.

disqualifyingIssues: Invented named characters (Bracken, Thistle, Doctor Bell)
Multiple invented dialogue expansions and plot flourishes
evaluations.rationale: Visually rich and clip-friendly staging is undermined by severe fidelity violation through invented proper names and non-source dialogue; cannot be green-lit as an adaptation of the book.

Otherwise strong visual storytelling and near-complete beat coverage are disqualified by the introduction of an invented proper name for a wild rabbit, triggering the mandated severe fidelity penalty.

judgeSummaryNotes: Strongest: Screenplay C because it delivers the most exhaustive, visually precise and clip-ready translation of every source beat with locked character descriptions. Weakest: Screenplay G because it jumbles chronology, invents events and collapses the narrative into an unusable fragment.
